class_guess: Skelet-like nested bouncer: walls between (01) runs, a left buffer, multi-level counter (no rule table yet)
summary: Head bounces between movable walls (extra 0s) in (01) runs; local rules exact, counter level and proof open
mechanism: Every E left record is K(n; a) = 0^inf <E 01^n 0 01^a1 0 ... 0 01^aL 0^inf: a buffer of n pairs (n+1 per cycle), then walls (single extra 0s); true at all 223,095 records to 1e11.

Leftward E/F sweeps close open walls and bounce at the first closed one (L3); rightward A/F or C/D phases shift a wall (R5), open it (R6, R7) or turn back (R8, R9, R11). 20 local rules, 6,000/6,000 checks.

a_j is exactly 2^(j+1)-periodic in cycles (j = 1..8) and the right end is reached at doubling intervals: a counter hierarchy. Halts seen only from a1 = 0, n odd; on the orbit a1 is 7 or 8. Twin: line 612 (start E).

template.diff: different table; #3 has digit blocks s(d) = 0001/0010 and one sweep per decrement, this machine has single-cell walls and nested bounces
template.note: Only #3's proof plumbing carries over: sweep lemmas folded over a block list (RP/LP, PassesR/PassesL) and progress_nonhalt_cond with an invariant. Its macro rules (Dec_k, DecMerge, End, Ov, X1, X2) have no counterpart; here a cycle is a nested bounce over walls, not one decrement.

strategy: Next: a wall-level abstract simulator built from R1-R11/L1-L3 plus the right-end routine, checked against the TM to 1e11; derive the cycle map on (n; a) and the carry hierarchy. Then either an invariant (a1 >= 1, wall spacing) with progress_nonhalt_cond, or a closed-tape-language certificate (robust: no halts from random K with a1 >= 1).
risks: No macro (cycle-level) rule yet: one cycle is a nested bounce whose depth depends on the whole wall vector; the right-end routine reads a long left context.
The settled digits (7 13 25 9 3 10 9 6 34 ...) have no closed form yet, so an inductive invariant may need a new idea.
25 busycoq CTL parameter sets (NG n-gram 4-24, RWL_mod, CPS_LRU) found no certificate; 4 hit the 6 GB cap.
